FINDING_ID: IM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.89  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim exports `DynamicManager` only from `_manager.py`, but the same module docstring states `_manager.py` contains immune-boundary symbols `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, `_apply_transform`, and `process_round`. Since the analytical boundary explicitly includes those manager-level immune integration points, the shim breaks boundary-level backward compatibility for any consumer importing those names from `dynamic_management`. Evidence: the orchestrator import block is exactly `from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401`; no import of `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, or `_apply_transform` appears. Prior findings covered this generally, but the missed cross-cutting part is that this prevents external tooling from inspecting or testing the remediation chain definition that coordinates `DetectorHealthMonitor` outputs with config mutations and `process_round()` integration.  
FIX: Re-export the manager-side immune symbols named in the file’s own inventory. Exact code replacement:  
<<<<
# ── Orchestrator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._manager import DynamicManager  # noqa: F401
====
# ── Orchestrator ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._manager import (  # noqa: F401
    DynamicManager,
    _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
    apply_diagnosis,
    _apply_transform,
)
>>>
FOLLOW: Re-exporting these names creates two downstream obligations. First, the shim should define an explicit `__all__` including these symbols, otherwise backward compatibility remains accidental. Second, if `apply_diagnosis` and `_apply_transform` are instance methods rather than module-level functions, this exact import will fail; in that case the docstring inventory is wrong and must be corrected instead of re-exporting them. FOLLOW: the codebase therefore needs a consistency pass between `_manager.py` symbol ownership, docstring inventory, and any tests/imports expecting flat access via `dynamic_management`.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Re-export `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, and `_apply_transform` from `_manager.py` if they are module-level symbols; otherwise correct the module inventory to state they are `DynamicManager` methods only.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The immune review boundary in the shim docstring excludes `_failure_handler.py`, but the user’s analytical boundary explicitly includes `FailureHandler`, and the shim’s own “Immune layer” imports include `FailureHandler` and `CorrelatedFailureModel`. This is not just a doc mismatch: it misassigns ownership of immune responsibilities across subsystems. In the supplied interface summary, `FailureHandler` is the component that consumes config (`timeout_multiplier`, `theta_under`, `n_fail`, `persistence_window`, `eta_underperform`, `k_min`) and emits `ManagerEvent`s, making it one of the main cross-subsystem couplers between immune logic, config, eventing, and role assignment. Excluding it from the review boundary hides the config-to-recovery path. Evidence: docstring says `The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.` while imports include `from bench.dm._failure_handler import FailureHandler, CorrelatedFailureModel`.  
FIX: Correct the boundary statement to include the failure-handler module. Exact text replacement:  
<<<<
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _manager.py.
====
The immune layer review boundary is: _types.py + _immune.py + _failure_handler.py + _manager.py.
>>>
FOLLOW: Once `_failure_handler.py` is explicitly inside the boundary, the artifact must also expose or document `FailureRecord`, `FailureType`, `RecoveryAction`, `ManagerEvent`, and the event-callback contract as immune-relevant dependencies. FOLLOW: this also strengthens the need to include actual failure-handler implementation slices in the artifact package; otherwise the stated boundary and the delivered code remain inconsistent.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Update the boundary statement to include `_failure_handler.py` and supply that module’s implementation in the review artifact.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim exports `DetectorDiagnosis` from `_types.py` while exporting `DetectorHealthMonitor` from `_immune.py`, splitting the immune diagnosis contract across two modules without documenting that split. The missed cross-cutting issue is ownership ambiguity: reviewers are told to focus on “DetectorDiagnosis, DetectorHealthMonitor, apply_diagnosis(), and immune config parameters,” but the only artifact implies the diagnosis type lives in generic shared vocabulary rather than the immune module that produces it. That obscures the interface between diagnosis production and diagnosis application, especially when the implementation body is unavailable. Evidence: `from bench.dm._types import ... DetectorDiagnosis ...` and separately `from bench.dm._immune import DetectorHealthMonitor`. No comment or contract explains why the diagnosis type is housed outside the immune module.  
FIX: Clarify module inventory and import grouping so the type-to-producer relationship is explicit. Exact text replacement in the module inventory section:  
<<<<
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (all shared vocabulary)
    ...
    _immune.py             DetectorHealthMonitor (immune detection layer)
====
    _types.py              Config, enums, dataclasses (including DetectorDiagnosis,
                           the diagnosis record consumed by manager-side remediation)
    ...
    _immune.py             DetectorHealthMonitor (immune detection layer; produces
                           DetectorDiagnosis instances)
>>>
FOLLOW: This fix has documentation and testing consequences. Any external code or tests constructing `DetectorDiagnosis` directly now has an explicit contract that it is an immune-consumed type, not generic vocabulary. FOLLOW: if the real implementation instead defines `DetectorDiagnosis` semantics inside `_immune.py` and merely stores the dataclass in `_types.py`, the artifact package should include both the dataclass definition and all construction sites; otherwise semantic fields remain under-specified.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document explicitly that `_immune.py` produces `DetectorDiagnosis` and `_manager.py` consumes it, even if the dataclass lives in `_types.py`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

DESCRIPTION: FIND: The artifact omits any explicit public contract for immune config parameters even though the analytical boundary includes “immune config parameters” and the interface summary identifies them as behavior-driving knobs shared across `FailureHandler`, `DetectorHealthMonitor`, and `process_round()` integration. The shim re-exports only the entire `DynamicManagementConfig` type; it does not surface or document which fields are immune-owned versus globally shared. This is a cross-cutting omission because immune changes can affect convergence thresholds (`tau_sim`, `tau_vocab_growth`), prompt injection (`per_model_directives`), decomposition strategy (`pre_decompose_models`), and failure escalation (`timeout_multiplier`, `n_fail`, etc.), but none of that ownership is visible in the artifact. Evidence: the artifact imports `DynamicManagementConfig` only as part of a bulk `_types` re-export, and the module docstring inventory does not identify immune-related config fields or where they are consumed.  
FIX: Expand the module inventory/docstring to identify immune-owned config fields and their consuming modules. Exact text insertion after the `_manager.py` inventory line:  
<<<<
    _manager.py            DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
                           apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)
    _validation.py         validate_all_reductions
====
    _manager.py            DynamicManager (orchestrator, _REMEDIATION_CHAINS,
                           apply_diagnosis, _apply_transform, process_round)

across modules:
    _failure_handler.py -> timeout_multiplier, theta_under, n_fail,

                           tau_vocab_growth, per_model_directives,
                           pre_decompose_models
>>>
FOLLOW: This fix exposes a downstream design obligation: config fields that are mutated by immune logic but consumed by non-immune detectors need stable ownership semantics and likely dedicated tests for round-to-round consistency. FOLLOW: if any listed field is not actually consumed where documented, that discrepancy will become visible and should be corrected in `_types.py` comments or the implementation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document the immune config field surface and its per-module consumers directly in the shim/module inventory.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.68  
FLAW_CLASS: 2  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: FIND: The shim flattens immune-layer and non-immune-layer exports into one namespace without any explicit grouping API, but the task’s analytical boundary depends on tracing interactions between components. This flat export style is a missed cross-cutting defect because it obscures subsystem seams: `DetectorHealthMonitor`, `FailureHandler`, `ManagerEventStream`, `RoundProgressionFSM`, `ConvergenceDetector`, `DiminishingReturnsDetector`, and `DynamicManager` all become peers at import time despite having distinct dependency directions. Evidence: every symbol is imported into module top level; there is no `immune` namespace, no `__all__` subgrouping, and no comments tying exported symbols to producer/consumer relationships beyond coarse section headers.  
FIX: Add an explicit `__all__` that preserves flat compatibility while making subsystem ownership machine-readable. Exact code insertion at end of file:  
<<<<
from bench.dm._validation import validate_all_reductions  # noqa: F401
====
from bench.dm._validation import validate_all_reductions  # noqa: F401

__all__ = [
    # Types/config
    "DynamicManagementConfig",
    "Role",
    "CapabilityFingerprint",
    "ModelSpec",
    "Task",
    "Finding",
    "FailureType",
    "RecoveryAction",
    "FailureRecord",
    "ModelResponse",
    "DetectorDiagnosis",
    "State",
    "Event",
    "TerminationReason",
    "ManagerEventType",
    "ManagerEvent",
    "RoundResult",
    "FindingEquivalenceClass",
    # Areas
    "RoleAssignment",
    "Allocation",
    "LoadBalancer",
    "RoundProgressionFSM",
    "ConvergenceDetector",
    "DiminishingReturnsDetector",
    # Immune
    "DetectorHealthMonitor",
    "FailureHandler",
    "CorrelatedFailureModel",
    # Events
    "ManagerEventStream",
    # Orchestrator / validation
    "DynamicManager",
    "_REMEDIATION_CHAINS",
    "apply_diagnosis",
    "_apply_transform",

>>>
FOLLOW: Adding `__all__` has two consequences. First, it forces resolution of whether `_REMEDIATION_CHAINS`, `apply_diagnosis`, and `_apply_transform` are actually importable as top-level names; if not, the export list will fail and expose the inconsistency immediately. Second, if private convergence helpers are intentionally not public, they should be removed from `__all__` and likely from top-level imports too. FOLLOW: this turns implicit API drift into explicit testable breakage, which is the correct failure mode for a compatibility shim.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Add explicit `__all__` grouped by subsystem, including the actual immune public surface and excluding incidental internals unless truly supported.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: IM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 4

DESCRIPTION: FIND: The artifact and interface summary together leave the eventing boundary under-specified for the immune subsystem. `FailureHandler` emits `ManagerEvent`s via `event_callback(event)`, and the shim separately exports `ManagerEventStream`, but the actual relationship is absent from the artifact. The missed cross-cutting issue is ownership of failure telemetry: immune behaviour depends not only on remediation but on whether failure events are reliably captured, and the current artifact presents eventing as a separate section detached from the immune boundary even though `FailureHandler` depends on it. Evidence: import sections separate “Immune layer” and “Event stream”, while the interface summary says `FailureHandler` calls `event_callback(event)`; no comment states whether `event_callback` is typically `ManagerEventStream.emit`, a bound method, or an adapter.  
FIX: Amend the event-stream section comment to declare its runtime relationship to the immune layer. Exact text replacement:  
<<<<
# ── Event stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401
====
# ── Event stream ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Runtime dependency note: FailureHandler emits ManagerEvent instances through
# an event_callback compatible with ManagerEventStream consumption.
from bench.dm._events import ManagerEventStream  # noqa: F401
>>>
FOLLOW: This fix implies the implementation artifact should include the callback adapter or binding site in `_manager.py`; otherwise the contract remains only partially specified. FOLLOW: if `ManagerEventStream` is not the intended consumer, then the interface summary is misleading and should be corrected to name the real callback target.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Document the runtime coupling between `FailureHandler` and `ManagerEventStream`, and include the binding site in the manager implementation artifact.  
VERIFIED: TRUE
